prose.text:
A small drop of water often looks rounded.
The surface of a liquid tends to become smaller.
The pull along this surface is called surface tension.
When other pushes and pulls are weak, surface tension helps shape small drops.

Gravity pulls water downward as we pour it into a cup.
The way the water flows and the cup's material also affect what happens.
Surface tension is part of this story, not the only cause.
The pull of stretched objects and the rubbing force called friction are other forces we meet.
Surface tension can have a strong effect on small drops, even when we hardly notice it in a full cup.
prose.source_text: 在我们周围，除了万有引力、弹性力和摩擦力以外，还存在有一种我们通常不注意的力. 这个力是比较小的，它的作用通常也不引起人们的注意. 然而，没有现在谈的这个力起作用，我们就不能往杯子里斟水，就根本不能作跟任何液体有关的事情. 这个力就是表面张力.

prose.text:
Surface effects appear in soap bubbles and in writing with ink.
A dip pen picks up ink from an inkwell, a small ink bottle.
Some older fountain pens store ink in a sac, a small ink-holding bag.

Water or ink can spread over a material and stick to it.
How much it spreads and sticks is called wetting.
Ink stays on a pen or flows out partly because of surface tension.
The pen's shape, material, and wetting also matter.
Soap on our hands and foam, a group of bubbles, involve liquid surfaces.
A place where liquid meets air or another material is called an interface.
Wetting and the materials involved help decide how soap spreads and foam lasts.
Fine drizzle is rain made of tiny drops.
Whether it quickly soaks a fabric also depends on wetting and the fabric.

Surface tension also helps shape drops involved in rainbows.
A rainbow needs sunlight to bend and reflect inside drops and separate into colors.
Surface tension also affects water in tiny openings, called pores, in soil.
Plants take water from soil.
Their water supply depends on the soil and the plant as well as surface tension.
prose.source_text: 我们对表面现象所引起的效果，已经习以为常了. 如果我们不吹一个肥皂泡来作消遣游戏，就不会注意它们. 然而，在自然界和日常生活中，这些效果起很大的作用. 没有它们，我们就不能用墨水写字，沾水钢笔就不能从墨水瓶里沾墨水，吸水钢笔吸进的墨水就会立刻从皮囊里倒出，弄成一个很大的墨斑；手上将不能擦上肥皂，不能形成泡沫；毛毛细雨也会湿透我们的身体；在任何天气都看不到虹；土壤给植物供水的条件将被破坏，植物将死亡.

prose.text:
Water drips slowly from a faucet, also called a tap, when it leaks.
The opening where water leaves the tap is called the outlet.
A drop grows at this opening and hangs downward.

A thin part of the drop still joins it to the tap.
This thin part is called the neck.
As the drop grows, the neck becomes thinner.
The drop then breaks away and falls (Figure $67$).
The attached drop is still joined to the faucet.
The detached drop is no longer joined to it.
Gravity pulls downward, while surface tension pulls along the drop's surface.
The flow of water also affects when the neck narrows and breaks.

The surface can pull a little like a stretched elastic film.
An elastic film is a thin layer that can stretch and spring back.
This is only a comparison.
The drop contains water, not water inside an elastic bag.
Its surface is not a shell made of some other material.
When the neck separates, no solid skin tears.
prose.source_text: 最简单的，在观察没有关好或失修的水龙头流出的水滴时，可以看到表面张力的性质. 仔细地观察水滴是怎样逐渐形成的：下坠变窄——下部突出，上部变细——水滴落下（图 $67$）. 不难设想，水好象是装在有弹性的口袋里，当它的坚固性不能支持大量水的时候，这个口袋就被拉断. 当然，实际上水滴中除了水以外，什么也没有. 但是，水的表面层好象是一个被拉伸的弹性薄膜.

prose.text: Figure 67
prose.label: 图 67

prose.text:
A soap bubble blown on a straw can stay joined to the straw.
Its wall is a thin layer of soapy liquid, called a liquid film.
It looks a little like the thin rubber wall of an inflated ball.
The bubble wall is liquid, not solid rubber.

If you take the straw from your mouth, its open end can let air out.
The bubble must stay joined to the straw, with a clear way for air to leave.
Surface tension can then shrink the liquid wall as air escapes.
A sealed bubble has no open way for its air to leave.
This explanation of shrinking needs an open way out for the air.
prose.source_text: 肥皂泡的薄膜也给人以同样的印象. 它好象是吹胀的皮球的薄橡皮外壳. 如果从嘴里取出麦杆，肥皂泡排出它里面的空气，就逐渐缩小.

prose.text:
A needle placed carefully on water can sometimes stay at the surface.
The water's surface curves down beside the needle.
Part of the pull along this curved surface points upward.
That upward pull can help support the needle.
The water under the needle also pushes upward.
This upward push from the water is called buoyancy.
Support also depends on wetting, or how water spreads over and sticks to the needle.
If these upward forces cannot support the needle, it sinks.
Careful placement helps, but it does not guarantee that every needle floats.

Water striders are small, light insects that move over water.
The surface pull and the water's upward push can support them near the surface.
They can look like skaters moving over ice.
The water beneath them is still liquid, not ice or a solid sheet.
prose.source_text: 小心地把一只针放在水面上. 表面层薄膜弯曲，而针并不沉没. 同理，轻小的昆虫——水黾，可以很快地沿着水面爬过去，就象滑冰运动员滑冰一样.

prose.text:
A sieve is a mesh with small holes for things to pass through.
When water is poured gently into some fine-mesh sieves, it can stay there briefly.
The water's surface curves across the small holes.
Surface tension helps this curved surface hold back the water.
Whether this works depends on the hole size and wetting.
Wetting means how water spreads over and sticks to the mesh.
It also depends on pressure, or how hard the water pushes.
Larger holes or a harder push can let the water through.
Some sieves cannot hold water at all.

Woven fabric is made from threads that cross each other.
The fibers are the thin strands that make up those threads.
The tiny openings between threads and fibers are pores.
A curved water surface can delay water passing through some of these openings.
The result depends on the strands and how water spreads over and sticks to them.
Water can get through if the openings are too large to hold it back.
It can also get through if it spreads easily into the fabric or pushes too hard.
Some fabrics let water through right away.
prose.source_text: 把水轻轻地倒在很密的筛子里，水的薄膜变弯，水并不会流出来. 纺织品也是一种筛子，它是用线编织的. 表面现象使得水通过它是很困难的，因此，纺织品不能立即漏水.

prose.text:
A free drop does not rest against a solid surface.
Its surface tends to become smaller while it holds the same amount of liquid.
This unchanged amount is called a fixed volume.
If other pushes and pulls are weak, the drop becomes nearly ball-shaped.
The word spherical means ball-shaped.
Gravity and nearby flowing air or water can change the drop's shape.
Compare drops of the same liquid in similar surroundings.
For smaller drops, surface tension usually has more effect on shape compared with gravity.
Small dewdrops can look nearly spherical.
They touch a solid surface, so spreading and sticking there still affect their shape.

A falling raindrop is pulled down by gravity.
Falling freely does not stop air from pushing against it.
This push from air is called air resistance.
Small raindrops can be nearly ball-shaped.
Larger raindrops can be flattened or otherwise changed by the air.
Raindrops are not all perfect balls.

A rainbow forms when sunlight enters water drops under suitable conditions.
Refraction means the light bends as it enters or leaves a drop.
Internal reflection means the light reflects from inside the drop.
Dispersion means sunlight separates into different colors.
Nearly ball-shaped drops help produce the familiar rainbow.
Drops need not all be perfect balls for a rainbow to appear.
prose.source_text: 如果不受地球吸引作用，由于表面膜有缩小的趋势，液体将呈球形. 水滴越小，表面力比体积力（吸引力）起的作用越大. 因此，小露珠近似球形. 物体在自由降落时产生失重状态，因此，雨滴几乎是球形. 由于太阳光线在这些水滴中的折射产生了虹. 水滴若不是球形，也没有虹.

prose.text:
Inside a spacecraft, liquid can float in a near-weightless setting.
This setting is called microgravity.
Gravity is still present.
Small drops and larger blobs can become nearly ball-shaped if they are away from solid walls.
This happens when flowing liquid and other pushes disturb them only a little.
The surface pull must matter more for their shape than competing pushes and pulls.
Touching a wall or being stirred strongly can give the liquid a different shape.
prose.source_text: 在处于失重状态的宇宙飞船中，不仅单个的水滴而且质量较大的液体，也都呈球形.

prose.text:
A liquid is made of tiny particles called molecules.
They keep moving and can pull on nearby molecules.
Think of a group gathering into a close cluster.
This comparison helps us picture the outside surface of a drop becoming smaller.
For a free drop, that can bring its shape closer to a ball.
Molecules do not make plans or choose to gather.
Walls and other forces can still affect the drop's shape.
prose.source_text: 表面张力的显示，可以这样来解释：如果一大群个体具有彼此吸引的性质，或者，每个个体都想彼此靠近，结果它们将缩成一团. 每个个体都“力求”在这个团的内部，于是团的表面就缩小，接近于球形.

prose.text:
Liquid molecules pull on each other and keep moving.
Molecules near an interface have different neighbors from those deep inside the liquid.
An interface is where the liquid meets air or another material.
The combined pulls depend on each molecule's neighbors.
They need not pull every surface molecule in the same direction.

Surface area means the amount of outside surface.
Making more of this surface takes extra energy when certain things stay steady.
Temperature, or how hot or cold the liquid is, must stay nearly the same.
Composition, or what the liquid is made of, must also stay nearly the same.
The neighboring air or other material must stay nearly the same too.
Under these conditions, the liquid can settle into a shape with less surface area.
Other forces must be weak, and walls must not hold it in a different shape.
For the same amount of liquid, a ball has the least surface area.
This is why a free drop tends to become spherical, or ball-shaped.

Molecules keep moving and changing places, which lets liquid flow.
Even when a drop settles into a steady shape, its molecules keep moving.
They move in many directions, rather than all traveling inward forever.
prose.source_text: 彼此相互吸引的水分子或其他液体分子，“力求”接近. 表面上的每个分子都受到液体内部其他分子的吸引. 因此，它们具有往深处浸入的趋向. 因为分子从一个“定居的”位置跳到另一位置，液体要流动，所以它们取表面上分子数最少的形状. 而在一定体积下，最小的表面是球. 所以液体的表面收缩. 这就是表面现象.

prose.text:
Stretched rubber can pull less strongly as it gets shorter and less stretched.
This comparison applies while the rubber can still spring back normally.
A liquid's surface pull comes from its molecules, not from stretched solid rubber.
The pull for the same length of edge can stay nearly the same as the surface gets smaller.
This is described by a number called the surface tension coefficient.
An edge here is a line across the surface where we consider its pull.
We compare equal lengths of this line, not the pull along every possible edge.
The liquid and the neighboring material must stay the same.
The temperature and what the liquid is made of must stay nearly the same too.
The conditions where the liquid meets that material must also stay nearly the same.
The coefficient then does not decrease just because the surface gets smaller.
The total pull along an edge can still change if its length changes.

Gently squeezing most liquids changes their volume, or the space they fill, very little.
This is called being nearly incompressible.
Density tells us how much material is packed into a given space.
If the amount of liquid and its volume stay almost the same, its density also stays nearly the same.
The gaps between molecules then stay about the same on average.
Density is not fixed under all conditions.
Changing the temperature, pressure, or conditions at the surface can change it.
prose.source_text: 这里应注意，表面力的起源完全不同于被拉伸的橡皮膜的弹性力. 当橡皮收缩时，弹性力减小，而表面张力不随着表面膜的收缩而改变，因为液体的密度并不改变，从而表面上分子间的平均距离也不改变.

data.chapter: 第五章　液体的表面现象
data.title: 表面现象

prose.text: 在我们周围，除了万有引力、弹性力和摩擦力以外，还存在有一种我们通常不注意的力. 这个力是比较小的，它的作用通常也不引起人们的注意. 然而，没有现在谈的这个力起作用，我们就不能往杯子里斟水，就根本不能作跟任何液体有关的事情. 这个力就是表面张力.

我们对表面现象所引起的效果，已经习以为常了. 如果我们不吹一个肥皂泡来作消遣游戏，就不会注意它们. 然而，在自然界和日常生活中，这些效果起很大的作用. 没有它们，我们就不能用墨水写字，沾水钢笔就不能从墨水瓶里沾墨水，吸水钢笔吸进的墨水就会立刻从皮囊里倒出，弄成一个很大的墨斑；手上将不能擦上肥皂，不能形成泡沫；毛毛细雨也会湿透我们的身体；在任何天气都看不到虹；土壤给植物供水的条件将被破坏，植物将死亡.
最简单的，在观察没有关好或失修的水龙头流出的水滴时，可以看到表面张力的性质. 仔细地观察水滴是怎样逐渐形成的：下坠变窄——下部突出，上部变细——水滴落下（图 $67$）. 不难设想，水好象是装在有弹性的口袋里，当它的坚固性不能支持大量水的时候，这个口袋就被拉断. 当然，实际上水滴中除了水以外，什么也没有. 但是，水的表面层好象是一个被拉伸的弹性薄膜.
肥皂泡的薄膜也给人以同样的印象. 它好象是吹胀的皮球的薄橡皮外壳. 如果从嘴里取出麦杆，肥皂泡排出它里面的空气，就逐渐缩小.
小心地把一只针放在水面上. 表面层薄膜弯曲，而针并不沉没. 同理，轻小的昆虫——水黾，可以很快地沿着水面爬过去，就象滑冰运动员滑冰一样.
把水轻轻地倒在很密的筛子里，水的薄膜变弯，水并不会流出来. 纺织品也是一种筛子，它是用线编织的. 表面现象使得水通过它是很困难的，因此，纺织品不能立即漏水.
如果不受地球吸引作用，由于表面膜有缩小的趋势，液体将呈球形. 水滴越小，表面力比体积力（吸引力）起的作用越大. 因此，小露珠近似球形. 物体在自由降落时产生失重状态，因此，雨滴几乎是球形. 由于太阳光线在这些水滴中的折射产生了虹. 水滴若不是球形，也没有虹.
在处于失重状态的宇宙飞船中，不仅单个的水滴而且质量较大的液体，也都呈球形.
表面张力的显示，可以这样来解释：如果一大群个体具有彼此吸引的性质，或者，每个个体都想彼此靠近，结果它们将缩成一团. 每个个体都“力求”在这个团的内部，于是团的表面就缩小，接近于球形.
彼此相互吸引的水分子或其他液体分子，“力求”接近. 表面上的每个分子都受到液体内部其他分子的吸引. 因此，它们具有往深处浸入的趋向. 因为分子从一个“定居的”位置跳到另一位置，液体要流动，所以它们取表面上分子数最少的形状. 而在一定体积下，最小的表面是球. 所以液体的表面收缩. 这就是表面现象.
这里应注意，表面力的起源完全不同于被拉伸的橡皮膜的弹性力. 当橡皮收缩时，弹性力减小，而表面张力不随着表面膜的收缩而改变，因为液体的密度并不改变，从而表面上分子间的平均距离也不改变.

section_breaks.before:
The textbook also mentions rainbows and the supply of water from soil to plants.
Surface tension affects droplet shapes and water in tiny pores, but rainbows also require suitable optical conditions, and plants' water supply depends on more than surface tension alone.
These examples show the importance of surface phenomena without implying that changing surface tension alone must cause every consequence listed in the original.
section_breaks.after:
Watching water drip slowly from a tap that is not fully closed or needs repair illustrates surface tension.
A droplet grows and hangs downward;

section_breaks.before:
As a temporary analogy, we can compare the water's surface to a stretched elastic film.
The droplet is not inside a real elastic bag, and its surface is not a shell made of another substance.
The neck's separation is not the tearing of a material skin.
section_breaks.after:
A soap bubble can also look as though it has the thin rubber skin of an inflated ball.
But its wall is a liquid film, whose properties should not be equated with those of solid rubber.
The textbook describes a bubble gradually shrinking as air escapes after a straw is taken from the mouth.

section_breaks.before:
Woven fabrics also have pores between their threads.
Surface phenomena can delay water passing through some fabrics, but the result depends on the fibers, pore sizes, wetting, and water pressure.
It is not a general rule that all fabrics prevent immediate leakage.
section_breaks.after:
For a freely suspended droplet of fixed volume, surface tension favors a nearly spherical shape when deformation by gravity, external flow, and contact with solid surfaces can be neglected.
For the same liquid under comparable conditions, surface effects usually become more important relative to gravitational deformation as droplets get smaller.
Small dewdrops can be nearly spherical, although wetting of the surface they touch still affects their shape.

section_breaks.before:
In a spacecraft's near-weightless, or microgravity, environment, freely suspended liquid away from container surfaces can form nearly spherical droplets or larger blobs when flow disturbances are small.
This still requires surface effects to dominate the shape.
Liquid touching a container wall or strongly disturbed by flow does not necessarily become spherical.
section_breaks.after:
The textbook compares surface contraction to a group of mutually attracting individuals gathering into a cluster.
The analogy suggests how the surface can become smaller and the shape approach a sphere.
It does not mean that molecules intentionally seek the interior, or that boundaries and external forces can be ignored.

section_breaks.before:
This equilibrium picture does not mean that every surface molecule moves inward forever.
Molecules continue their thermal motion.
section_breaks.after:
Liquid surface tension has a different origin from the elastic force in stretched rubber.
Within the relevant elastic range, rubber's pull can decrease as it contracts and its stretch decreases.
For the same liquid and adjoining medium, when temperature, composition, and interface conditions remain nearly unchanged, the surface tension coefficient does not change with shrinking surface area in the way rubber's pull changes with stretch.
